cards.title: The culture surrounding 'ideal' childbirth has to evolve
cards.body: Letters responding to an article about a five-day labour highlight how cultural expectations around childbirth need to change. NHS doctors share personal experiences of feeling 'othered' by prevailing attitudes toward different birth experiences.

cards.title: I've forgotten so much about parenting a second baby
cards.body: A parent reflects on how much knowledge fades between children, from feeding to teething to sleep. Family support, especially from grandparents, becomes invaluable when navigating forgotten milestones.

cards.title: Parenting is hard. Should we let AI do it for us?
cards.body: Tech companies now offer eye-movement trackers, personalized podcasts and 'optimized nap predictions' for parents. The question remains: who actually needs these tools, and what are we outsourcing?

cards.title: Should I try the '18 summers' parenting trend?
cards.body: The '18 summers' trend pushes parents to optimize school holidays into scheduled memory-making. Long, unstructured days may be more valuable than turning childhood into a controlled experience.

cards.title: Passing the Torch of Anxiety
cards.body: Children can absorb parental anxiety about fear and uncertainty. Small changes in how parents respond to fear can break this cycle and build confidence in children.

cards.title: The thoughts mothers are afraid to tell you about
cards.body: Postpartum journals reveal the darkest thoughts mothers experience but often hide from shame. Creating safe spaces for honesty about maternal struggles can be crucial to recovery.

cards.title: ADHD Burnout in Kids, Teens, and Young Adults
cards.body: Children with ADHD may struggle with motivation and emotions beyond typical ADHD symptoms, signaling burnout. Parents can recognize these signs and provide targeted support to help their child recover.

cards.title: The hidden cost of providing too much comfort
cards.body: Excessive comfort can actually hinder children's growth when they're struggling. Kids need space to work through discomfort to develop resilience and problem-solving skills.

cards.title: Autism and Vaccines: Questions Science Hasn't Settled
cards.body: The debate over autism and vaccines continues in public discourse. Rather than winning arguments, the focus should be on making evidence-based decisions for child safety.

cards.title: Needing Others Doesn't Make You Needy
cards.body: Healthy relationships support well-being and autonomy in children and adults alike. The key is understanding the difference between healthy interdependence and unhealthy reliance on others for self-worth.
